name: Learn: Multi-cluster Contexts
objective: CKA exam-environment skill: every task tells you which cluster to use via `kubectl config use-context`. Goal: work across TWO real clusters — create resources on the right one, never the wrong one, and always know your active context.
description: The #1 silly way to lose exam marks is running a correct command on the wrong cluster. This lab gives you two real clusters (kind-kindlab and kind-kindlab2) and makes you target each deliberately.

questions.title: Switch context and act on the right cluster
questions.teach:
`kubectl config use-context <name>` switches the **active context** — the cluster every later `kubectl` command lands on. Here you have `kind-kindlab` (`$CTX`) and `kind-kindlab2` (`$CTX2`). Switch to cluster2, then create normally.

**Gotcha:** confirm the switch with `kubectl config get-contexts` — the `*` marks the active one; a correct command on the wrong cluster grades wrong.
questions.prompt:
Switch to the **second** cluster and create a namespace `prod` **there** (on `$CTX2`), not on cluster1.

Target: namespace `prod` exists on cluster2 and does NOT exist on cluster1.
questions.hint: `kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab2` then `kubectl create namespace prod` — or in one shot: `kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 create ns prod`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab2
kubectl create namespace prod
kubectl config get-contexts   # confirm the * is on kind-kindlab2

questions.title: Deploy onto cluster2
questions.teach: Create a Deployment imperatively with `kubectl create deployment --image= --replicas=`. Scope it to one cluster and namespace in a single safe command: `kubectl --context $CTX2 -n prod create deployment ...`. **Gotcha:** omit `-n` and the Deployment lands in the context's default namespace (usually `default`), not the one you meant.
questions.prompt:
On cluster2, create a Deployment `api` (image `nginx:alpine`, 2 replicas) in the `prod` namespace.

Target: Deployment `api` with 2 replicas exists in `prod` on cluster2.
questions.solution: kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 -n prod create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2

verification.description: Deployment 'api' (2 replicas) in prod on cluster2

questions.title: Now work on cluster1
questions.teach:
Switching back to cluster1 is just another `use-context kind-kindlab`. Create a ConfigMap imperatively with `kubectl create configmap <name> --from-literal=key=value` (repeat `--from-literal` for more pairs).

**Gotcha:** the clusters are fully independent — the ConfigMap you make here on cluster1 does NOT exist on cluster2.
questions.prompt:
Switch to **cluster1** (`$CTX`) and create a ConfigMap `shared-cfg` with key `env=prod` in the `default` namespace **there**.

Target: `shared-cfg` (env=prod) exists on cluster1 and NOT on cluster2.
questions.hint: `kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab` then `kubectl create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab
kubectl create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod

questions.title: Replicate a resource across clusters
questions.teach:
To copy a simple resource to another cluster, just recreate it imperatively on the target — cleanest when you know its contents: `kubectl --context $CTX2 -n prod create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod`.

**Gotcha:** the `--context` and `-n` here target cluster2/`prod` explicitly; without them the ConfigMap would go back to your active context instead.
questions.prompt:
Replicate `shared-cfg` (env=prod) into the `prod` namespace on **cluster2**.

Target: ConfigMap `shared-cfg` with `env=prod` exists in `prod` on cluster2.
questions.hint: Simplest: `kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 -n prod create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod`.
questions.solution: kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 -n prod create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod

verification.description: shared-cfg (env=prod) exists in prod on cluster2

questions.title: Context discipline — know where you are
questions.teach:
Finish each task by leaving your active context where the *next* one expects, then verify with `kubectl config current-context`. Here, set it back to cluster1 with `kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab`.

**Gotcha:** `use-context` persists to the kubeconfig file, so your choice survives into the next task's shell — set it deliberately rather than assuming.
questions.prompt:
Leave your **active** context set to cluster1 (`$CTX`).

Target: `kubectl config current-context` returns `kind-kindlab`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab
kubectl config current-context   # kind-kindlab
